text: OVERDOSAGE One case of deliberate overdosage with ticlopidine has been reported by a foreign postmarketing surveillance program. A 38-year-old male took a single 6000-mg dose of ticlopidine hydrochloride (equivalent to 24 standard 250-mg tablets). The only abnormalities reported were increased bleeding time and increased SGPT. No special therapy was instituted and the patient recovered without sequelae. Single oral doses of ticlopidine at 1600 mg/kg and 500 mg/kg were lethal to rats and mice, respectively. Symptoms of acute toxicity were GI hemorrhage, convulsions, hypothermia, dyspnea, loss of equilibrium and abnormal gait.
